{What is left over goes to a stranger before dark, and the stranger is not told | Bury the wax where three paths meet, and never go back to look at the place | The same materials never serve two people, and the practitioner remembers whose was whose until death}.

1034: {The dart asks the body to kneel, and the body obeys | Not every quarry is meant to die; some are meant to be carried home}. {Breathe out, measure the weight, let the dose fly | Aim for the thick of the shoulder and the beast will dream before it falls}. {Sleep, and wake in chains | Lie down. 1036: {A hand on the shoulder, a word in the ear, and the shaking stops | The dazed soldier is not lost while a comrade still sees clearly}. {Clear your eyes. Find the front sight. 1038: {The fowler's gun was meant for the flock | Buckshot keeps no favourites and spares no one in its cone}. {Fill the air and they will flinch from it | The spread only chooses}. {Scatter, and be slow | Let the lead find the ones who ran}.
1039: {The first shooter marks, the second ends it; the Finnish ski patrols hunted that way through the winter of 1940 | One rifle names the target so that every rifle may answer}. {Fire to mark, and let the squad finish the sentence | Where my round strikes, all of yours will follow}. {There. 1040: {Zaitsev waited three days in the ruins for one shot, and he took it | Patience is the deadliest weapon a ranger carries}. {Let the world grow still. Let the heart slow. 1041: {The Lewis gunners of 1916 said a man is swept | Speed is a discipline too, and it has its own masters}. {Short bursts. Keep the muzzle down. Walk it across them | Four shots in the space of one heartbeat, and four in the next}. {Rattle and roar | Let them hear the drum}.
1042: {The steel core was made for the grandsons of the knight, who still trust in plate | No shield was ever forged that a patient maker of bullets could not answer}. {Behind the shield there is a man. 1043: {The archers of Agincourt darkened the sky; we inherited the sky | Fire high and let it fall. 1044: {Every round in the belt is different, and every one was chosen | The best and rarest of the quartermaster, saved for the hour that deserves them}. {Spend it all. 1045: {At Rorke's Drift a hundred rifles held against thousands, firing until the barrels scorched the hands | A barrage is a wall built of lead, one brick at a time}. {Keep firing. Do not count. 1046: {Every beast has its seam: the joint, the throat, the gap beneath the arm | The old hunters of the Alps learned where the chamois breaks, and taught no one else}. {Find the place the armour forgets | Fire at the flaw in the body}. {There is your opening | Now he bleeds where he cannot guard}.
1047: {The British square fired by ranks, and the charge broke upon the smoke | Ready. Present. Fire. Three words older than any of us}. {On my word, every rifle at once | One voice, one crack, one wall of fire}. {Volley, and again | Again, before they rise}.
1048: {A shell is a small sun carried in a brass case | The grenadier's craft was to throw fire; ours is to fire it}. {Lead the target, then lead the blast | Let the round burst among them, and let the flame do the rest}. {Burn, all of you | The ground itself turns against them}.
1049: {Pavlichenko counted three hundred and nine, and every one began with stillness | Häyhä lay in the snow with no scope, so that no glint would betray him}. {One shot. 105: {Zazen: just sitting. 1050: {Xenophon kept his hounds before he kept his horses, and named every one of them | The Molossian hound walked beside the legions and was buried with honours | Before the bow there was the pack, and the pack has never forgotten it}. {Run with me, brother. 1051: {The ranger marks the quarry the way a smith marks hot iron: once, and for good | The mark is a promise, and every ranger keeps it}. {Wherever you run, the crosshairs have already been | I have named you. The rifle will remember}. {Marked, and finished | No cover will hide you now}.
1052: {When the line is broken and the enemy is close, no art is left but the trigger | The trench fighters of Verdun emptied the magazine}. {Plant your feet. Hold the recoil with your whole body. 106: {The jab is the fastest punch there is, and the masters of the ring call it the most important | Muhammad Ali said float like a butterfly, sting like a bee, and the jab was the sting}. {Faster than the eye, faster than the thought | No feint, no wind-up, only arrival | Before you see it, it has landed}. {There. 1065: {The Mongol rider ate in the saddle and never once slowed the column | Bread in the left hand, rein in the right: so the legions crossed Gaul | A soldier who waits for the table is a soldier who waits for death}. {Salt for the blood, sugar for the legs, and no time wasted on either | Eat now. 1066: {Locusta served the enemies of Nero at his own table, and none of them refused the plate | Every cook knows the line between nourishment and ruin, for every cook has walked it | What the kitchen can raise, the kitchen can bring down}. {Rot is patient. 1067: {Avicenna kept honey beside the knife, and trusted it more | The apothecaries of Venice sweetened the theriac, for no cure works that cannot be swallowed | Before sugar was pleasure it was medicine, and the old masters never forgot it}. {Let the sweetness draw the poison out as heat draws out the frost | Whatever was taken into the body, this takes back}. {Eat, all of you. 1068: {Bodhidharma cut away his eyelids to stay awake, and where they fell the first tea grew | Lu Yu wrote the Classic of Tea so that no mind would ever again be poured out carelessly | Rikyu taught that the whole Way lives in boiling water and a bowl}. {Water short of the boil. 1069: {The cauldron of the Dagda sent no company away unfed, however many came | The pot of the legion was carried behind its eagle, for an empty army is a dead one | A stew is the oldest oath a cook can swear: no one at this fire goes hungry}. {Bone, root and fire, given the whole night to become one thing | It is slow. 107: {Sok trong, the straight elbow of Muay Thai, falls on the head like a hammer on a nail | The old fighters of Siam aimed the elbow at a skull already ringing}. {Strike where the last blow landed | A head already shaken does not hold the second time | The elbow drives straight down the centre}. {Again, on the same place | The bell is already ringing for you}.
1070: {The cooks of Constantinople stood on the walls beside the archers, and their cauldrons did the greater killing | Every keep had its kitchen above the gate, and every kitchen knew why | Water given to fire long enough becomes a weapon that no armour turns}. {The stock has rolled since dawn. Let it roll over them | Scald the ranks; the steam will find the rest}. {What I throw does not miss by much | Stand in the doorway, then, and be served}.
1071: {The Tudor kitchens baked gold leaf into the crust and set the pie before a king | Scappi wrote that the finest pie is the one that raises the guest from his despair | A golden crust is a promise made to the dying}. {Rise. 1072: {From the murder holes of every castle in Christendom fell oil and flame, and the siege broke beneath them | Callinicus gave Byzantium a fire that water could not kill, and the cooks kept the secret after the engineers were dead | Oil is patient in the pan and merciless out of it}. {Bring it to smoke. Then past smoke | Let the fat take flame, and let the flame take the field}. {Burn, all of you, and know whose kitchen you entered | No water will save you. Water was never the cure for this}.
1073: {The knife of the butcher has fed the butcher since the first beast fell | Two cuts: one for the enemy, one for the hand that holds the blade | What the edge opens, the cook takes for the cook}. {Quick, low, twice. The body remembers where the meat is | Every wound I give is a meal I keep}. {Your strength becomes mine, one slice at a time | Cut, and be fed}.
1074: {Maimonides prescribed the broth of a hen to the Sultan himself, and the Sultan lived | In the long northern winters the soup pot never left the fire, for the fire was all that kept the frost from the door | Broth was the first medicine, and it is still the surest}. {The warmth goes down and does not leave | Ice breaks in the throat and melts in the chest}. {Drink, and let the heat keep working after the bowl is dry | Winter does not come to this table}.
1075: {Cook Ding carved oxen for nineteen years and never sharpened his blade, for he cut only where the beast was already open | The cleaver is the oldest weapon of the kitchen, and was a weapon long before it was a tool | The master finds the joint}. {Weight in the tip, faith in the arm | One fall of the iron, and the work is done}. {I have broken down a thousand carcasses. You are one more | The board is wet. Lie still}.
1076: {At the Symposium the wine was poured and the mind set free; so Plato learned what love was | Escoffier held that the table is where a nation remembers who it is | Those who break bread together think as one, and fight as one}. {Sit down, all of you. 1077: {There is a kitchen beneath the crossroads, and the one who cooks there asks a price of the cook alone | The Grand Grimoire names a supper that feeds armies and sickens the hand that served it | Some recipes are bargains, and the cook always pays first}. {Eat, brothers. 108: {Yip Man taught the chain punch as the heart of Wing Chun: straight, continuous, down the centreline | The chain punch is a river of fists, and no dam holds a river}. {Six blows on one line, and the line does not break | Each fist rides the one before it | The guard cannot rise against the flood}. {Straight down the middle | Until the arms come down}.
1089: {Hush, all of you, and lie down in the dark | Sleep, host of the field, sleep as the dead sleep | Close your eyes, every one, the night has come for you}. {The singer pays the song its due, and the song may take the singer too | Hypnos takes the whole rank and does not ask whose voice called him}. {This is the cradle song the old masters sang over battlefields | No watch is kept where this lullaby is heard}.
109: {Imi Lichtenfeld learned to fight in the streets of Bratislava against those who came for his neighbours | Krav maga has one principle: defend and attack at the same moment}. {Your attack is my opening | The block is the strike | The faster you came, the harder you return}. {That was a mistake | Bring it, and I take it from you}.
1090: {Rest now, the voice says, and the throat is bared | A mother's song with a blade folded inside it}. {The Sirens sang to Odysseus of rest, and the bones on their shore remember | The gentlest note is the one that opens the guard}. {Sleep, and show me where you break | When you wake, if you wake, you will know what you gave me}.
1091: {Diabolus in musica, the interval the choirmasters forbade | Play the notes that were struck from the hymnals}. {The world was sung into being, and what is sung can be unsung | Orpheus moved stones with a lyre; this is the other song he knew}. {Their strength, their skin, their speed and their spirit, all out of tune | Let the ground beneath them forget its own key}.
1092: {Three notes, played true, and the line holds | The first song every apprentice learns is the one that keeps them alive}. {Plant your feet; the tune will carry the rest | A plain melody, steady as a heartbeat under armour}.
1093: {Again, the hall demands, and the company answers | The curtain does not fall while one of us still stands}. {What the fight took, the second chorus gives back | Draw breath, take up the measure, and begin once more}.
1094: {Stage Presence. Spoken once. Indoors. By one voice. Never again by the same mouth. | There is one thought in this room, and it is sharper than any blade in it. | Reaching is for hands. I attend, and distance kneels.} {Those who hear it are the instrument. Without them, nothing here moves. | The voice is raised, the rhythm is struck, and every heart in reach keeps time. | The song is the working. Sung true, it commands the field.} {It works on anything with a mind, and the dark has always had one. | Information moves and nothing else does. That is enough to break a world. | every enemy breaks where every enemy is thinnest, and the mind always knows where that is.}
1095: {The band falls silent and the stage is mine | Step out of the line, alone, into the light}. {Every scale I ever practised, every night I bled for it, now | The hands know what the mind dares, and the mind follows}.
1096: {The night has a song, and it is older than the moon | Draw the dark down over their eyes like a veil}. {Chopin wrote his for the salon; this one was written for the hunt | Let the shadows lengthen until they cannot find their own hands}.
1097: {Strasbourg, the summer of 1518, and the dancers would not stop | The tarantella was danced to drive the venom out; this one draws the life in}. {Watch me move, and feel your strength leave you to feed it | Every step I take is paid for in your blood}.
1098: {Sing, and the power in them rises to the sound like water to the moon | The galdr of the North was always sung, and it took what it named}. {Your gift answers my voice now | Give me your fire, all of you, verse by verse}.
1099: {Hush, little warrior, the battle is done for you | Lay down the sword; the song has already won}. {One voice, one listener, and the eyes grow heavy | Nurses sang this over cradles long before soldiers learned to fear it}.
110: {Tui shou, push hands, is the test of the taiji player: listen to the opponent through the skin | The Chen family taught that four ounces may deflect a thousand pounds}. {Feel the push, yield, and return it doubled | Their root lifts; mine does not | Four ounces, and the thousand pounds go elsewhere}. {Off your line | I listen, and the force flows on}.
1101: {To know, to dare, to will, and to keep silent; this is the fourth | Pythagoras bound his students to five years without a word}. {Let every tongue in the field forget its spells | The silence is the song, and it is louder than any cry}.
1102: {Two notes a breath apart, held until the air itself cracks | Strike the chord that no cathedral would allow}. {Every blessing laid on them shakes loose at the sound | The walls of Jericho were not breached with rams}. {Let it ring; nothing they built will stand inside it | Hold the discord, and the world will break first}.
1103: {The sound turns on itself and screams | Let the voice run back into the voice until it howls}. {Hit them before they can cover their ears | A wall of noise, thrown like a fist}.
1104: {Hear them roar, and take that roar into your chest | The crowd is the fire, and we are the forge}. {Every cheer is strength, every chant is breath | Rome built the Colosseum because the roar was worth an army}.
1105: {All eyes on us, and not one of us will falter | Stand tall; the light finds those who claim it}. {The great ones never looked at the crowd; they looked through it | Command the stage and the mind grows sharp as a blade}.
1106: {Sing it with me, the song our fathers marched to | The drums beat once, and every heart beats with them}. {Tyrtaeus sang Sparta into battle, and Sparta did not run | No one falls alone while the chorus holds}.
1107: {Up, and up, and up, and then down on their heads | Three pins in the air and one is meant for you}. {The jongleurs of the fairs threw knives as easily as apples | Watch the hands, and you will never see the throw}.
1108: {Into the corner, and the corner does not give | Iron post, steel cable, and you between them}. {This is the ring, and the ring answers to no one | Break the guard against the ropes and leave it broken}.
1109: {Not yet; the count has not reached ten | Get up, all of you, the bell has not rung}. {The body has one more fight in it, and it was saving that one for now | Breathe in, and feel the old strength come back hard}.
111: {Sapuan, the sweep of silat, is performed low enough to touch the earth | The pesilat of Minangkabau learned to fight on the slick floors of the rice terraces}. {One turn, low to the ground, and every leg is taken | The circle of the foot passes under all of them | Rob them of the ground, and they are slow}. {Every one of you, down | Stand up slowly. You will}.
1110: {Whispers under the hearing, in a tongue that has no grammar | A murmur from behind, though nothing stands behind them}. {The mind turns to listen and cannot turn back | The bards of Eriu raised blisters with a satire; this cuts deeper}.
1111: {Look at me, the voice says, and there is no choice but to look | One line, delivered right, and pride does the rest}. {The fools of the old courts spoke truths that kings could not leave unanswered | Come and silence me, if you can}.
1112: {Lift, arch, and bring the heavens down on him | The bridge holds, and the man on it does not}. {Milo of Croton carried the bull; carry this one into the mat | The title is earned on the back of every man thrown}.
1113: {Up with the moon, then over and down like its falling light | Turn in the air as the moon turns in the sky}. {Nothing that flies is beyond the reach of one who flies higher | Come down on them from where they thought they were safe}.
1114:
{I find the mind of Enthralling Melody's quarry and I close my own around it. | I speak the Performance words inwardly, slow as a pulse, heavy as a verdict. | I set down my name. Where I am going, names are a weight.} {The voice is raised, the rhythm is struck, and every heart in reach keeps time. | Those who hear it are the instrument. 1119: {Everything, all of it, now, and nothing held back | The last act, the full company, the whole house burning bright}. {Three times the music swells, and three times it falls on them | There is no encore after this, and none is needed}.

113: {The body scissors is the python's grip, practised by the wrestlers of the Punjab akharas | The legs are three times as strong as the arms, and they close like a vice}. {Cross the ankles and squeeze until the ribs give | The breath goes out, and nothing comes back in | Bound in the coils, the body weakens}. {Breathe out. 1131: {Look upon the foe until the foe is laid bare | Sun Tzu taught it first: know the enemy, and a hundred battles hold no peril | Every wall has one stone set badly; the captain finds it before the siege}. {Name the flaw aloud and the whole company strikes it | What has been seen cannot hide again}.
1132: {Print his name in black and every hand turns against him | The heralds of old named the traitor at the city gate, and the city did the rest | A reputation falls faster than any wall}. {He is marked, and the mark does not wash off | From this hour he bleeds for every blow}.
1133: {One voice, loud as a trumpet, and the dreamers wake | Stentor of the Achaeans shouted with the voice of fifty men | The war shout breaks every spell laid on a soldier's mind}. {On your feet, eyes front, hands on steel | Wake, and remember whom you serve}.
1134: {The one who cries first is the one the enemy sees | Tyrtaeus sang the Spartans into the line, and the line held | A battle cry is a banner made of breath}. {Let them come at me; you strike while they do | My voice for your blades, my body for your shield}.
1135: {Pericles spoke over the dead, and the living stood taller | We few, we happy few: the words outlast the king who spoke them | A speech is slow, and it is the strongest thing a leader owns}. {Hear me to the end, and then go and do it | What I say now, you will carry into the blow}.
1136: {Divide and rule: Rome wrote it on every border she held | One word dropped among enemies does the work of a legion | Machiavelli taught that a divided foe defeats himself}. {Let them doubt each other, and their hands will slow | The seed is small; the harvest is their ruin}.
1137: {Shield to shield, the phalanx is one beast with a hundred hearts | The Sacred Band of Thebes never broke, for no man would shame the one beside him | Close the ranks; there are no gaps in a wall of brothers}. {Your wound is my wound, and we mend together | We stand as one, or we do not stand}.
1139: {The general sees the seam in the armour and names it for every blade | Vegetius wrote that the wise commander strikes where the enemy is not ready | Strategy is the art of choosing the single point}. {There. Strike there, all of you | One mark, and every hand finds it}.
114: {The low kick of Muay Thai fells a man the way an axe fells a tree, one blow at a time | The fighters of Siam conditioned their shins on the trunks of banana trees}. {Into the thigh, and the leg forgets how to stand | The shin is the axe | Every blow to the leg sets up the next to the head}. {The tree is falling | This is the first. 1140: {The envoy walks between the armies and no spear is raised | Heralds carried the staff of Hermes, and to strike one was sacrilege | Lay down your sword first, and the enemy will lower his}. {I come under the white sign; let no hand touch me | Peace is a shield only the bold can carry}.
1141: {Look at me | The skirmisher dances before the line so the line may strike unseen | Horatius held the bridge alone, and every spear came to him}. {Come, all of you, if you can catch me | I am the lure, and I am never where your blade falls}.
1142: {The hero rises, and every soldier rises with him | Achilles returned to the field and the Trojans broke at the sound of his voice | When all seems lost, the true commander is first seen}. {Now, all of you, as one, as never before | Follow me, and be more than you are}.

1148: {Caesar spoke to the Tenth, and the Tenth would have followed him into the sea | A soldier fed on purpose marches farther than one fed on bread | The fire is lit with words and burns through the whole battle}. {You were made for this day | Keep faith, and your strength will not run dry}.
1149: {Stand tall, say nothing, and let him feel the weight of it | The Spartans combed their hair before Thermopylae, and the Persians were afraid | Fear is a blade that cuts before the steel is drawn}. {Kneel, or be made to | His arm grows heavy under my stare}.
