{Come back. The work is not finished with you | Breathe. I have not given you leave to go | Stay. The field still needs you standing}.
1937: {Three legs, one eye, no mercy | Plant the gun and hold the ground}. {Sweep left, sweep right, and again | Gatling built it to end war; it ends fights}.
1938: {Wire to wire, plate to plate | Mend the armour and the soldier mends himself}. {Back in the line | What the field breaks, the field repairs}.
1939: {Wait, and let them come to the wire | The trap is patient; be the trap}. {One step, and the lightning has him | Ground beneath them, thunder within them}.
194: {The berserker wears no armour, because armour is for those who expect to survive | Odin's warriors went mad as dogs or wolves, bit their shields, and were strong as bears}. {The red comes down, and there is only the enemy | No pain, no fear, no tomorrow | Bite the shield, and break the line}. {Rage | Odin, take my fury}.
1940: {Steel joints for mortal knees | The brace moves before the blow lands}. {Faster than the eye, lighter than fear | Dance, and let them strike the air}.
1941: {Nothing is wasted in war | Load the wreckage and give it back}. {Let the scrap find its marks | Bolts, nails, iron: a storm of broken things}.
1942: {Past the red line, and further | The machine screams, and so do I}. {Burn bright, burn now | The breath comes back; the moment does not}.
1943: {Liechtenauer wrote it in rhyme so the scholar could not forget it: the strikes first, then the guards, then the strikes again | Fiore had his pupils cut the same line until the arm knew it before the eye | A thousand cuts at the pell, and the thousand and first is the one that counts}. {Again. Again. Again, until the hand forgets to ask | The form is learned in the arm | Cut, return, cut}. {The blade remembers what I forget | Let the steel decide}.
1944: {The instructors at Hythe taught the mad minute with an empty breech first, fifteen rounds that never left the barrel | Front sight, breath, squeeze, and the hammer falls on nothing | The range officer says the empty rifle is the best teacher, because it cannot lie about the flinch}. {Again, and do not blink | Sight, breathe, press. Sight, breathe, press | The hand learns what the bullet will not wait to teach}. {Now it is loaded | Now I am ready}.
1945: {On Okinawa the kobudo masters taught the sai, the tonfa and the nunchaku through the same kata as the empty hand | The weapon is only the arm made longer, said the old teachers of Shuri | Kata first, then the weapon, then the kata again with the weapon in it}. {The weapon moves as the hand moves | Breathe out on the strike, in on the return | Nothing new, only the form made longer}. {Hand and weapon are one | The form holds}.
1946: {Steuben drilled the army at Valley Forge with a handful of English words and many more in German | The sergeant does not ask whether you are ready; he tells you that you are | Every army that ever held its ground was first shouted at on a parade square}. {Grip it like you mean it | Feet apart, eyes front, do it again | You know this. Your hands know this}. {Now do it as I showed you | By the drill, soldier}.
1947: {Maurice of Nassau broke the musket into forty two motions and had the whole company make each one on the same word | The Prussian line drilled until a thousand men moved like one, and the enemy saw a wall | On the parade ground everyone is a rank}. {As one. On my word. Again | Dress the line, and the line will carry you | Each of you is the drill, and the drill is all of you}. {Present arms | Hold the line together}.
195: {The spike drives the opponent into the canvas like a nail into a beam | Lift them high, and let the ground strike the last blow}. {Head first, and the earth does the rest | Down like a stake into the ground | The impact goes through the whole body}. {Spiked | Lie still. You have no choice}.
1958: {PSI Echo. Spoken once. Indoors. By one voice. Never again by the same mouth. | One mind for this company, shared by all of it. | I am quiet. I am quieter. I am [REDACTED], and the world goes still to hear it.} {The thought is aimed like a spear and driven through every wall of the skull. | Nothing here can be weighed. Will is the only blade. | The battle is fought inside a mind, and the mind is not always the caster's.} {It works on anything with a mind, and the dark has always had one. | It leaves the other no option of refusing. | Nothing crosses the space between, for there was never any space between.}
196: {The dragon fist is the culmination of the southern schools, fed by all the chi the fighter has stored | The dragon grows with what it devours, and the fist grows with the fight}. {All the fire of the fight, released at once | The more I hold, the more I give | The dragon wakes with everything it has}. {Dragon | Receive everything}.
1965: {The palm opens, and what was scattered in the body is called back to the centre | Breath in through the nose, down past the navel, and held there like water in a cupped hand}. {Strike, and keep what the strike returns | The blow is small; what it gathers is not}.
1966: {Nine breaths, and the ninth is the longest | The ribs are iron bands, and the breath is the fire inside them}. {Everything is made ready | The body is closed like a door before the storm}.
1967: {All that was gathered is given at once, and the hand is empty after | The dam is opened wide}. {What is held too long turns inward and sours | The old masters spent it all, and began again from nothing}.
1968: {The force that would have broken another is turned upon the self, and mends | The breath is sent where the hurt is, and told to stay}. {Nothing gathered is wasted | The wound is answered from within}.
1969:
{"No matter what the circumstances, it lies with us to master them, or to be mastered, as we will" (Heindel, The Rosicrucian Mysteries) | "I cried aloud the word - and it was a mighty spell to bind the Invisible, an enchantment to unbind the bound" (Crowley, The Holy Books) | "Alas, how a great people shall be tormented, And the Holy Law in an utter ruine" (the Prophecies of Nostradamus)}. {The seal is quartered, and no quarter closes until the one before it has been named aloud | The vault is opened with three knocks, and the third is struck with the pommel of the sword | The triangle of art is set outside the ring, and one enemy is written into it before anything is called}. {Something is commanded to stay, and it stays | The dead are near, they are many, and they are addressed as a host | The rot is spoken into the flesh, and the flesh begins to listen}. {The Name is spoken once toward each quarter, and at the fourth the air grows heavy as lead | The command is given in the imperative, repeated in the vocative, and never softened | The operator writes his own name on the parchment and strikes it through with one stroke}.

{Sulphur is thrown on the coals at the naming, and the curse rides out on the smoke | The seal is quickened with the breath, for ink alone is dead | Between the fourth and fifth name the floor is struck once with the heel, and the floor answers}. {wisdom is the oil the working burns, and the figure blazes for as long as it lasts | What is bound is loosed by the operator's word and by no other voice under heaven | What is sealed inside the ring leaves it altered in one particular, and soul reap names that particular in advance}.

{The apprentice writes the rite out from memory at dawn, and every error is burned with the page | Across {nation} it is held that the rite is sound and the operator is in peril | Where a fifth voice is heard and four stood, the work is stopped and not resumed that season}.
197: {The masters of the internal arts teach that chi can leave the body, and the strongest send it across a room | The cannon of the spirit is loaded with years of breath}. {Gather, compress, and release | The chi leaves my hands like a cannonball | Everything I am, fired at you}. {Fire | Hear it before you feel it}.
1970:
{"The force of fire, whose heat destroieth, it breaks and bringeth downe" (Scot, The Discoverie of Witchcraft) | "And when she is appeared, take your censers, and incense hir with frankincense, then bind hir with the bond as followeth" (Scot, The Discoverie of Witchcraft) | "I cried aloud the word - and it was a mighty spell to bind the Invisible, an enchantment to unbind the bound" (Crowley, The Holy Books)}. {A black stole, the sigil of Grave Tithe turned against the heart, and the lamp set where no shadow falls | A knife with a black hilt is laid on the altar for the cutting of the air, and the cursed is called to its edge | The vault is opened with three knocks, and the third is struck with the pommel of the sword}. {Something is commanded to stay, and it stays | The rot is spoken into the flesh, and the flesh begins to listen | The grave is opened, the bones are named, and the bones rise to the name}. {The alphabet is walked from the last letter to the first and halted at the letter of Necromancy | The charge is delivered without pause, for a pause is a question, and the powers answer questions | Every drop of wisdom is poured into the figure like oil into a lamp, and the figure takes light}.

{The ninety-nine names are told over on the knuckles, and the hundredth is withheld | Every syllable is counted, and an even count means a syllable fell, and the whole is begun again | The command is given in the imperative, repeated in the vocative, and never softened}. {What is bound is loosed by the operator's word and by no other voice under heaven | A debt is opened against the quarter of the cursed, and every enemy pays it at once, in the coin of the body | The intelligence is given a door so narrow that it arrives in the shape asked for, and strikes as it arrives}.

{The chalk is scraped away with the back of the knife, and the scrapings are burned in the hearth | The ash is gathered into a linen pouch and buried at a crossroads before the cock crows | The operator does not sleep until the sun has stood an hour above the hills}.
1971: {"Beauty and strength, leaping laughter and delicious languor, force and fire, are of us" (Crowley, The Book of the Law) | "For from these every depraved spirit departs, and when they are present, is entirely subverted" (Iamblichus, On the Mysteries) | "If the Exorcist have not a care, he will slay both him and his fellows" (the Goetia)}. {A black stole, the sigil of Soul Pyre turned against the heart, and the lamp set where no shadow falls | The operator fasts three days, bathes in cold water and puts on linen no other body has worn | Two lamps are lit, the second from the first, and both burn until the dismissal}. {Something is commanded to stay, and it stays | The dead are near, they are many, and they are addressed as a host | The grave is opened, the bones are named, and the bones rise to the name}. {The blow lands as a debt called in, the debtor having been written into the seal at its making | The figure holds until the dismissal is spoken, and not one breath longer | What is bound is loosed by the operator's word and by no other voice under heaven}.
1972:
{"On this shewed our Lord that the Passion of Him is the overcoming of the Fiend" (Julian of Norwich, Revelations of Divine Love) | "From fear of Him the fire burns, from fear of Him the sun shines" (the Upanishads) | "And let great darkness cover over them, and let come to them an obscurity of darkness" (Pistis Sophia)}. {The lamp is lit at the fourth hour, and what is said in its light is not taken back | I call upon thee, {deity}, by the Name that was spoken before there was air to carry it | Anicca, dukkha, anatta. Three words, and Litany stands upon the third}. {What is holy in it belongs to no one present and only passes through | The radiance falls, and darkness has nowhere left to stand | It is gentle with what it blesses and merciless with everything else}. {Turn the mala toward the body, never away, and let each bead fall like a sentence | Sit until the sitting is no longer a posture. Then begin | Count the mantra on one hundred and eight beads, and never count the bead of the teacher}.

{The prayer is heard before it is said. The saying only opens the door | Emptiness is room made ready, and litany is what fills it | Judgement is lent for the length of litany and returned whole}. {The relic kept at {city} is said to have been touched by the first who spoke it | In {nation} it is taught after three years of the practice and never before | Leave the candle burning until it goes out of itself}.
1973:
{"And all my members in which there is not light moving, thou gavest to them a light of life from thy Height" (Pistis Sophia) | "O thou Only One, O thou Perfect One, O thou who art eternal, who art never weak, whom no mighty one can abase" (the Egyptian Book of the Dead) | "Thou art the Governor of gods and of men and hast received the sceptre, the whip, and the rank of thy Divine Fathers" (the Egyptian Book of the Dead)}. {Nine prostrations before the first word, and the ninth is made with the whole weight of the body | Om mani padme hum. The jewel is in the lotus, and the wound closes around the jewel | Blessed be the hour, blessed the breath, and blessed the hand lifted in vigil}. {The covenant is older than the caster and it is not broken on the field | One holy name is spoken, and everything built on a lie falls silent before it | The light is asked for, and it descends in the shape of the asking}. {Count the mantra on one hundred and eight beads, and never count the bead of the teacher | Breathe in on the first syllable, out on the second, and let the third come of itself | Sing the psalm in two choirs, and let the silent choir carry the heavier half}.

{Sit until the sitting is no longer a posture. Then begin | Breathe on the wound three times, and on the third breath say the Name | Lay on the hands and do not move them. Pray for patience}. {The vow binds the caster, and the bound caster binds the world | Merit is passed on and never held. Held merit goes still | What is given here is given because it is asked}.

{Whoever teaches it first declares themselves unworthy, and means it | Where it has failed, sit the same hours again the following week, and again | The pilgrims of {city} still walk to the shrine where it was first answered}.
1974:
{"And all my members in which there is not light moving, thou gavest to them a light of life from thy Height" (Pistis Sophia) | "O thou Only One, O thou Perfect One, O thou who art eternal, who art never weak, whom no mighty one can abase" (the Egyptian Book of the Dead) | "Thou art unknowable, and no tongue can describe thy similitude" (the Egyptian Book of the Dead)}. {Out of the depths I have cried unto thee, and the depths have answered with thy voice | Bless, O Lord, this working of Holy Magic, which was never mine to own | Blessed be the hour, blessed the breath, and blessed the hand lifted in miracle}. {The light is asked for, and it descends in the shape of the asking | One holy name is spoken, and everything built on a lie falls silent before it | Heaven is answered, and the answer is fire and mercy both}. {Fast until the noon office, and offer the hunger without naming it | Raise the hands to the height of the heart, palms outward, and hold them there through the whole office | Breathe in on the first syllable, out on the second, and let the third come of itself}.

{Strike the bell at the beginning and let another hand strike it at the end | Sit until the sitting is no longer a posture. Then begin | Trace the sign of the cross over the force, and the force takes the sign}. {The self is set down for the length of the office, and what acts meanwhile is not the self | It answers when the one asking has stopped needing it to | Attention is the offering. Everything else on the altar is ornament}.

{Bow once to the altar and once to the door, and leave without turning | Gloria Patri, and the office is sealed | Om shanti, shanti, shanti. Peace above, peace below, peace in the one who spoke}.
1975: {Oak and ash and thorn, the three that never bowed: stand with me now. | Green thing, green thing, rise and hear the one who calls thee. | Sun at rising, sun at noon, sun at setting: three gates, and Drench passes through the one that stands open.} {Water finds the way in and takes as long as it needs. That is the method and the threat. | It carries, it drowns, it wears away, and it is the one substance doing all three. | The tide is called up out of the deep and it does not ask where the shore is.} {What is asked of a living thing is granted, and the granting costs that thing its blood. | The hare is only slower than the hawk, and the hawk is the law. | Winter does not hate the leaf. It takes the leaf all the same.}
1976: {Eleven kelvin across the width of a hand. That gradient is the whole apparatus. | Two bodies, one gradient. The cold one is one enemy, and the cold one always loses. | The specific heat of bone is 1.6 kilojoules per kilogram per kelvin. Everything that follows is arithmetic and ruin.} {The sky splits, and the split runs straight through the foe. | The charge is gathered, held one breath too long, and loosed along the path cleared for it. | It goes by the readiest path and spares nothing standing on that path.} {Flesh takes in faster than it can shed, and the surplus comes out as ruin. | The lightning is a quantity moved, and what is moved comes out of something close by. | Every fire is a fall. I only choose where it lands.}
1977: {Carnot set the bound. No working of Pyromancy has crossed it, and none will. | dS >= 0, and Flashpoint decrees that the increase is paid inside one enemy. | P = dW/dt. Shorten the interval, and the same work arrives as the fire.} {Everything it touches is changed in one direction, and there is no road back. | It comes in burning and leaves the field scorched long after the working ends. | The flame is fed, the flame is raised, and the flame is loosed upon the field.} {A difference is made, and every difference is a debt against the world. | The energy was here before me. Flashpoint is a valve, and I am the hand on it. | The colder body is one enemy, and the second law does the rest without another word from me.}
1978:
{p V = n R T. Five letters, and the one who holds the pen decides which of them yields. | The enthalpy is negative and vast. The sign is the promise, the magnitude the threat. | dS >= 0, and Rime decrees that the increase is paid inside one enemy.} {Water is patient, and ice is water that has ceased to forgive. | Heat is torn out, and what remains is the shape of the taking. | Cold is slow, and slow is its weapon: it arrives while the target still hesitates.} {Every degree that goes in comes out somewhere. I say where, and I say it once. | Let the ice cross in an instant. A little, fast, breaks the bone that a great deal, slow, would only warm. | As above, so below, in heat as in all things, and neither is asked.}

{Reversibility is a fiction of the page. In the field the working runs one way, and the caster ages with it. | Two hundred joules in one square centimetre does what two hundred joules in a room never could. | Power delivered exceeds what tissue can shed, and the excess appears as the failure of structure.} {Fire, go back to sleep. I will wake thee again, and I will pay again. | The furnace at {city} is banked, the grimorie is closed, and the grimorie is the more dangerous of the two. | The cold left behind takes an hour to lift, and things die in it that were never aimed at.}
1979: {Every engine is a fall from hot to cold. Flash Freeze is the engine, and the fall is steep. | The enthalpy is negative and vast. The sign is the promise, the magnitude the threat. | First law: nothing is made. Second law: everything is spent. Flash Freeze is worked in the narrow space between them.} {It arrives slowly and holds the field after the caster has left it. | Frost climbs the veins and the heart beats slower with every breath. | What is frozen is held, and it waits for the shattering.} {The sum is unchanged. Only the arrangement obeys me. | Every fire is a fall. I only choose where it lands. | My intellect is the fuel, and I burn it knowing what it is.}
198: {A champion's combination is two punches thrown by someone who has thrown each a million times | Joe Louis needed few punches, and each one was the whole of him}. {Two blows, and both of them are finishers | Slow to come, impossible to survive | Plant the feet, and let the champion speak}. {Two | That is why I wear the belt}.
1980:
{Work the wax warm and never hot. Hot wax runs smooth, and a smooth figure is no one | Choose the room with care. For as long as the work runs it is the other room, and whatever happens in it happens there | Nine inches of red thread, a nail from a shoe worn through on the road, and the parings of one fingernail}. {The vessel, the fire and the will, and the will is what turns lead to gold | Matter is dissolved to its first root and raised again in a nobler form | One substance is commanded to become another, and both resist until they break}. {Ten. If the candle gutters at the naming, stop. Begin again the next night with a new figure | Twelfth: breathe when the figure would breathe, and hold your breath when it would hold | Eleven. Let no second person into the room. Two witnesses make two likenesses, and two likenesses tear the thread between them}.

{First: set the figure where the light falls on it the way the light falls on the target at this hour | Fifth: keep the count aloud. The count is the only clock in the room, and the room must keep time with the target | Twelve. The working ends when the figure is destroyed, and not one breath before}. {The bond weakens with the days, swiftly at first and then not at all. What remains after nine days remains for life | Whatever is left in the room is drawn into the working. That is why the room is emptied first | The practitioner stands at the nearer end of the thread, and the thread does not care which end it pulls}.

{The thread is burned. The nail goes into water. The wax goes into the earth. In that order and no other | Should the target die while the work runs, be out of the room before the news arrives | The same materials never serve two people, and the practitioner remembers whose was whose until death}.
1981:
{The old tables of correspondence for Alchemistry are read once, then closed. The target is written only in the wax | Take something the target has worn against the skin. Cloth is good. Cloth they mended with their own hands is better | Choose the room with care. For as long as the work runs it is the other room, and whatever happens in it happens there}. {Matter is dissolved to its first root and raised again in a nobler form | What is separated is purified, what is purified is joined, and what is joined is reborn | The vessel, the fire and the will, and the will is what turns lead to gold}. {Fourth: turn the figure to face the way two enemies at random is facing, and correct it the moment you learn you were wrong | Second: say aloud what you will do, in the order you will do it, before you do any of it | Fifth: hold the figure over the flame until the wax sweats, and speak the target's name into the heat}.

{Two things that have touched go on touching, and the working uses that and nothing cleverer | The force travels along the bond, and the bond has no length | Walls, shields and distance are irrelevant. The force is already where the target is, because it was put there through the likeness}. {What is left over goes to a stranger before dark, and the stranger is not told | It cannot be done twice to the same person with the same object. The object remembers the first time | Should the target die while the work runs, be out of the room before the news arrives}.
1982:
{The likeness is made first. It must be the only one, however plain | Like calls to like, and the whole of Phosphorus Flare is the labour of making the call impossible to refuse | Take something the target has worn against the skin. Cloth is good. Cloth they mended with their own hands is better}. {Matter is dissolved to its first root and raised again in a nobler form | Ash is all it leaves, and the ash is still warm | It comes in burning and leaves the field scorched long after the working ends}. {Seven. Break the smallest of the objects last, and break it cleanly on the first stroke | Tenth: do not name the day aloud. The working must not know where in the week it stands | Third: drive the thread into the wax at the joint you mean, and drive it with the nail, never the thumb}.

{The figure is the target for as long as the room agrees that it is, and the room has been made to agree | The practitioner stands at the nearer end of the thread, and the thread does not care which end it pulls | Walls, shields and distance are irrelevant. The fire is already where the target is, because it was put there through the likeness}. {Nothing used in it may be sold. Whoever buys it buys the bond with it | Burn the figure. Burn it whole. A fragment left is a working left open | Wash to the elbow in cold water and let the hands dry in the open air}.
1985: {The knee carries the man; take the knee | Nobody runs on a shattered joint}. {Low and steady, below the line of the heart | Aim where the body bends}. {He will live. He will not leave | The chase ends here}.
1986: {The falconer knows: bring down the wing and the bird is yours | What cannot fly must stand and answer}. {Lead the flight by a hand's breadth | Loose on the downbeat}. {Ground it | The sky closes behind it}.
1987: {Behind the knee the cord runs shallow | The old cutpurses called it the beggar's cut}. {One pass of the edge, low and from behind | Kneel, and stay knelt}. {A man who cannot follow is a man already lost | Walk away; he will not}.
199: {Every grand master keeps one technique that is taught to no one, and dies with them or with a single heir | The secret is the place where every lesson meets}. {Three blows, and each one breaks a different thing | Guard, balance, and life, in that order | What I kept for this moment, I give you now}. {Few have seen this | Now you know the secret. It will not help you}.
1995: {The flat of the blade is a lesson, the edge is a verdict | Liechtenauer taught that the long edge is turned before the blow, never during it}. {I turn the edge and let it decide | Whatever I strike now, I open | No more bruises, only wounds}.
1996: {The masters of the Murder Stroke held the blade and struck with the cross | A sword turned round is a hammer that remembers it was a sword}. {You will wake from this | I hold the steel by its own edge, and I hold back | Down, but not gone}.
1997: {The Okinawan masters hardened the fingertips in sand, then in gravel, then in stone | Nukite goes through the door}. {Five fingers, one point | My hand is a spearhead now | What shield stops a needle}.
1998: {Shuto, the sword hand, is the oldest blade a fighter carries | The edge of the palm was tempered on boards before it was ever raised in anger}. {My hand forgets it is a hand | Every chop is a cut now | I am the knife}.
1999: {The door is the job | A good night at the club ends with everyone walking out, some of them carried}. {Out, and still breathing | You sleep it off on the pavement | Nobody dies on my shift}.
200: {Asura is the name for those who fight without expecting the fighting to end | The asura realm is one of six in the Buddhist wheel, home of the mighty consumed by a war they cannot win}. {Every wound feeds the wrath | The pain becomes the fire, and the fire takes everything | Burn the body, and let the fury out}. {Wrath | Let every one of them feel what I have felt}.
2000: {Every peasant army in history found its spear in the barn | The hay is moved with the point, never with the handle}. {Whatever I hold, I hold it point first | Tines forward, and walk | Through the straw, through the shield}.
2005: {The empty magazine falls; the full one climbs into the grip | Steel to steel, and the gun remembers its purpose}. {Count the rounds in the dark, by weight alone | A soldier is a man who reloads before he is told}. {Chamber, and breathe | The next one will not miss}.
2006: {An empty gun is still a weight of iron | When the last round is gone, the grip remains}. {Turn it in the hand and bring it down | The barrel answers what the bullet could not}. {Once, and hard | Let him wake not knowing where he fell}.
201: {The undisputed champion has fought everyone, and everyone has hurt him, and he is still standing | A champion is defined by what he survives}. {Every blow I took, I give back at once | Battered, bleeding, and more dangerous than ever | Down to the last breath, and this is the breath}. {Undisputed | Nobody takes this from me}.
2015: {"From the law which binds all being The man is freed who masters himself" (Silberer, Hidden Symbolism of Alchemy) | "She supples his wounds, and infuses fresh blood into his veins" (Godwin, Lives of the Necromancers) | "No matter what the circumstances, it lies with us to master them, or to be mastered, as we will" (Heindel, The Rosicrucian Mysteries)}. {The seal is quartered, and no quarter closes until the one before it has been named aloud | The ground is consecrated with water and then with fire, in the quarter the working answers to | The figure is drawn in one unbroken line, for a broken line is a door left open}. {Something is spent that the caster will answer for, at an hour not of their choosing | This is the working copied by hand in the dark, because no honest press would set it | The old prohibitions are broken one by one, and each one breaks something in return}. {The powers keep to the letter, and hold the letter above the intention | Power is forbidden to leave the circle, and the whole art lies in the forbidding | The rite compels whatever is present to declare itself, and to declare itself in the shape commanded}.
2016: {Seat the charge, cut the fuse to length, and strike the match away from the body | Two turns of fuse, no more, and the hand that lit it is already moving | The charge goes where the enemy stands closest to its friends}. {Never go back to a fuse that has stopped hissing | Count aloud, and be behind cover before the count ends | Whoever plants it answers for the blast, every part of it}.
2017:
{"Millions of years have passed over the world, I cannot tell the number of those through which thou hast passed" (the Egyptian Book of the Dead) | "My power looked out of the midst of the Chaos, and (out) of the midst of the darknesses" (Pistis Sophia) | "All things under heaven sprang from It as existing (and named)" (the Tao Te King)}. {Heal, Lord, what thou hast made. I have carried the asking to thy door | Bless, O Lord, this working of Holy Magic, which was never mine to own | Lord, thou hast made this body and thou knowest where it is broken. Mend it}. {The covenant is older than the caster and it is not broken on the field | One holy name is spoken, and everything built on a lie falls silent before it | The light is asked for, and it descends in the shape of the asking}. {Keep the hours: matins, lauds, prime, and at the hour of none speak vow of dawn | Breathe in on the first syllable, out on the second, and let the third come of itself | Raise the hands to the height of the heart, palms outward, and hold them there through the whole office}.

{It answers when the one asking has stopped needing it to | The prayer is heard before it is said. The saying only opens the door | The prayer moves the one who prays first, and through them everything else}. {Sadhu, sadhu, sadhu. It is well done, and it is done | {faction} has sworn to guard the rite, and its name is never spoken in it | Om shanti, shanti, shanti. Peace above, peace below, peace in the one who spoke}.
202: {The champion of the arena earned the wooden sword, the rudis, and his freedom with it | A free gladiator who returns to the sand is the most dangerous man in Rome}. {I have stood here a hundred times. Strike me and see | The arena is mine. Every blow returns to its sender | Break their armour, and wait for them to answer}. {Ave | The sand remembers its champion}.
2025: {The world grows still between two heartbeats | Breathe out, and let the clock forget you}. {The sights rise slowly, and the bullet waits for them | Every falling thing hangs in the air until the shot is sent}.
2026: {The shot is a line, and a line can be stepped over | Turn in the air while the air is still deciding}. {Land where the bullet was not sent | The body remembers the lesson before the mind does}.
2027:
{I set a thought about this company the way a hand is cupped about a candle. | In. Out. In. Out. On the fourth breath, the word they blacked out of every copy. | Where the attention falls, the world leans. Mine falls now.} {Nothing here can be weighed. Will is the only blade. | The battle is fought inside a mind, and the mind is not always the caster's. | One mind closes its grip on another, and neither grip is made of flesh.} {Hold it. Hold it. Hold it. The length is secret, and it is felt in the teeth. | Do not want it. Wanting is noise. Noise ends the working and sometimes the worker. | What is aimed at this company arrives as a thought first. Meet it there, while it is small.}

{The All is Mind. The rest of the sentence is above any mortal clearance. | Information moves and nothing else does. That is enough to break a world. | It works on anything with a mind, and the dark has always had one.} {The closing words were removed. I say nothing, and I count to eleven, and it ends. | Take the conviction back before sleeping. Left in place it is dreamed, and dreams spread. | Whatever answered is not followed. That is the rule, and the rule is why some casters grow old.}
203: {The dragon spirit lives in the fire, and the southern schools call it down into the fist | The dragon dances at the New Year with fire in its mouth, and the dragon fist dances the same way}. {Three strikes, and three fires | The dragon breathes through my hands | Burn, burn, burn}. {The dragon wakes | Fire follows the claw}.
2035:
{"The firmament which surrounds her is like a tower with twelve gates, and at every gate are twelve myriads of powers" (The Gnosis of the Light) | "Thou knowest, O Death, the fire-sacrifice that leads to heaven" (the Upanishads) | "Thou art the Governor of gods and of men and hast received the sceptre, the whip, and the rank of thy Divine Fathers" (the Egyptian Book of the Dead)}. {Veni, Creator Spiritus. Come, and do not come gently | The bell, the breath, the Name. Nothing else stands in Soul Bond, and nothing else is needed | Lord, I am not worthy. Say but the word}. {The working only lends speed to what the body already makes | The wound is named as a thing permitted, and the permission is revoked | Life is pressed back into the vessel, and the vessel is sealed against death}. {Count the mantra on one hundred and eight beads, and never count the bead of the teacher | Walk sunwise once around the company, in silence, and the circle is closed | Raise the hands to the height of the heart, palms outward, and hold them there through the whole office}.

{What is holy passes through the caster and is not diminished by the passage | A watchfulness guards the company, and watchfulness outlasts a wall | The vow binds the caster, and the bound caster binds the world}. {Om shanti, shanti, shanti. Peace above, peace below, peace in the one who spoke | The pilgrims of {city} still walk to the shrine where it was first answered | Ite, missa est. Go, it is sent, and what is sent does not return empty}.
2036:
{"My power looked out of the midst of the Chaos, and (out) of the midst of the darknesses" (Pistis Sophia) | "The firmament which surrounds her is like a tower with twelve gates, and at every gate are twelve myriads of powers" (The Gnosis of the Light) | "I came (close) to thee, O Light, because thou becamest light on every side of me, thou art delivering me and thou art helping me" (Pistis Sophia)}. {Holy, holy, holy, and the third holy is the one that shakes the threshold | Buddham saranam gacchami. I go for refuge, and I do not go alone | Anicca, dukkha, anatta. Three words, and Martyr Vow stands upon the third}. {The covenant is older than the caster and it is not broken on the field | Heaven is answered, and the answer is fire and mercy both | The light is asked for, and it descends in the shape of the asking}. {Raise the hands to the height of the heart, palms outward, and hold them there through the whole office | Breathe in on the first syllable, out on the second, and let the third come of itself | Name the company one by one, aloud, and leave no one out}.

{Emptiness is room made ready, and martyr vow is what fills it | The refuge is a vow, and a vow cannot be breached | The prayer is heard before it is said. The saying only opens the door}. {Where it has failed, sit the same hours again the following week, and again | Ite, missa est. Go, it is sent, and what is sent does not return empty | Give thanks afterward at the same length, whatever the outcome}.
2037:
{"And when she is appeared, take your censers, and incense hir with frankincense, then bind hir with the bond as followeth" (Scot, The Discoverie of Witchcraft) | "From the law which binds all being The man is freed who masters himself" (Silberer, Hidden Symbolism of Alchemy) | "Thou dost transform whom thou dost touch, so that they, even merit to bee called Gods" (Blaise de Vigenere, Of Fire and Salt)}. {Two lamps are lit, the second from the first, and both burn until the dismissal | A hair of the operator is laid under the northern candle, and it binds the caster to the circle | The vault is opened with three knocks, and the third is struck with the pommel of the sword}. {The dead are near, they are many, and they are addressed as a host | Grave-work: the veil is thin here, and the art is the weight leaned upon it | Something is commanded to stay, and it stays}. {The ninety-nine names are told over on the knuckles, and the hundredth is withheld | Every syllable is counted, and an even count means a syllable fell, and the whole is begun again | The operator turns three times sunwise between the invocation and the charge, and does not look behind}.

{The powers keep to the letter, and hold the letter above the intention | wisdom is the oil the working burns, and the figure blazes for as long as it lasts | The ward stands because the figure is whole, and the figure is whole because nothing in it was hurried}. {The oldest copies close with one line: not twice within one moon | Nothing eaten for a day before, nothing spoken for an hour after | {faction} keeps the true figure under seal in {city} and lends it to no one}.
2038: {The shield is raised before the oath is finished | Hoplites of the old line stood for the man at their left | A captain is the first wall and the last}. {Strike them and you strike me | I stand here so that they need not}.
2039: {By the wolf that knows no sorrow and the winter that knows no mercy, Aeromancy is opened. | I call the year by its four names, and it turns its face to me. | Mother of the furrow, spread thy cloak over these, and let nothing find them.} {The air is already moving. The art is to seize its direction. | Wind is pressure given a will, and pressure is what breaks gates. | Something is pressed upon until it gives.} {A hedge stops more than any wall, being alive and unwilling to yield. | The words only keep time while the working is done. | What is asked of a living thing is granted, and the granting costs that thing its blood.}
204: {Qigong is the cultivation of the breath, practised by the Daoists for two thousand years | The masters say a single practitioner can steady a whole room with breath alone}. {Breathe with me, all of you | The chi flows from one body to every body | Let the current heal the whole circle}. {Together, we stand | Every breath, a little more whole}.
2040: {Rain that has fallen, rain that falls, rain that will fall: I set my hand in all three. | By root, by rind, by leaf, by seed, and by the fifth thing that has no name in any mortal tongue. | By the wolf that knows no sorrow and the winter that knows no mercy, Aeromancy is opened.} {Wind is pressure given a will, and pressure is what breaks gates. | The sky draws one breath and lets it out as a gale. | The air is already moving. The art is to seize its direction.} {What the mountain holds, it holds through every age. For this hour it holds the company. | The world takes no sides. It leans, and the lean decides the matter. | The field was fighting long before the first sword was forged, and it has never lost.}
205: {The ultimate finisher is the sum of the whole fight, every hold and blow and throw that came before | A fighter who has been broken in many places breaks all at once}. {Everything you suffered, paid in full | Every wound is a door, and every door opens now | The fight ends here, and it ends with this}. {Finished | All of it, at once}.
206: {The final reckoning is the strike the masters warn about: no defence can stop it, and no body survives giving it unscathed | Burn the chi to the last ember, and send it through the enemy}. {No armour, no guard, no escape | I give everything, and it costs me everything | This is the debt, and it is paid in full}. {Reckoning | No more}.
207: {The Battlemages of the old orders learned to carry the lightning in their hands, and closing the hand released it | Galvani made the dead frog's leg twitch with a spark, and the Battlemage makes the living one stop}. {The grip closes, and the current runs | Sparks in the palm, thunder in the arm | Hold, and let the lightning do the rest}. {Feel the current | The circuit is closed}.
208: {The life-binding strike ties the enemy's life to the user's, and what one loses the other takes | The Tibetan masters spoke of the thread that binds every living thing, and of the hands that can pull it}. {Your life, bound to mine | The blow lands, and the strength crosses over | What leaves you, enters me}. {Bound | You weaken, and I rise}.
209: {The acrobats of the Peking Opera trained from childhood to tumble through any space | The tumbler is never where the blade arrives, and never quite where he aims}. {Roll, flip, and vanish into the shadow | They strike the air I left behind | Hard to hit, harder to catch}. {Catch me | Gone again}.
210: {Om mani padme hum: the jewel in the lotus, chanted by the monks of Tibet to calm every mind | The mantra of peace is the strength to remain still when everything burns}. {Peace in the body, peace in the mind | The madness falls away, and the breath returns | Chant, and the storm inside goes quiet}. {Om | Calm. Whole. Ready}.
211: {Three jabs, and the fight is set: the boxer's oldest rhythm | The Marquess of Queensberry wrote the rules, and the jab wrote the fights}. {Pop, pop, pop, and the rhythm builds | Each jab is a step toward the knockout | The jab is the rangefinder. The rest is coming}. {Rhythm | Keep it moving}.
212: {The final paradise is the last technique of the old schools, a strike that ends the fight in a vision | Those who receive it say they saw a garden before the darkness}. {One blow, and the gates open | Off balance, and then into paradise | The last thing you will see is beautiful}. {Paradise | Rest now, at the end of the road}.
213: {The tiger claw of Hung Gar rakes and tears, and the tiger dance strikes every foe in reach | The tiger is the first of the five animals, and the most feared}. {Claw, claw, claw, and every wound bleeds | The tiger dances through the herd | Rake them all, and leave the marks}. {The tiger hunts | Bleed for the tiger}.
214: {The acrobat fights in the air, where the earthbound cannot follow | Whoever floats has left the ground, and the ground was their only defence}. {Up, into their sky | No one is safe in the air with me | I take the high ground, and it is all high ground}. {Up here, I am king | Fall}.
215: {The chakras are the seven wheels of the subtle body, and the forbidden strike turns them against their owner | The yogis teach the chakras to heal. The forbidden masters teach them to break}. {Strike the wheel, and the body spins out of order | The energy turns against itself | One blow to the centre, and the balance is gone}. {Unbalanced, inside and out | Your own wheels turn against you}.
216: {The liver shot is the one punch no amount of courage can stand through | The boxers say a man can take a hundred blows to the head, but one to the liver and the legs refuse}. {Under the ribs, on the right side | The breath goes, the strength goes, the will goes | Dig in, and take everything they have}. {Down on one knee | The body quits before the mind}.
217: {The Battlemages turned chi outward in a wave that struck every foe at once | The masters of the internal schools taught one breath for one target; the Battlemage taught one breath for all}. {The wave rolls out and every guard bends | Chi like a tide over all of them | One breath, and the whole line weakens}. {Onslaught | Feel the tide}.
218: {Ki is the breath of life in the Japanese arts, and mastery is the power to take it from others | The Battlemage drinks the enemy's power through the strike, and gives it to the next one}. {The wave lands, and their power flows to me | Unbalanced, and emptied | Your spirit feeds mine}. {Mastery | What was yours is mine}.
219: {The acrobat's flurry is a dance of many blows, thrown from every angle in a single tumble | The circus performers of Europe trained in the ring, and some of them went to war}. {Flip, strike, flip, strike, and I am never there | Through all of them, and none can catch me | Tumble, and the blows fall from the air}. {Too fast, too many | Gone before you turn}.
220: {The monk's fury is rare, and terrible when it comes | The Shaolin monks fought the pirates of the coast in the Ming era, and the coast remembers}. {Four strikes, and none of them calm | The peace is set aside for this | The temple's anger falls on the head}. {Fury | Even the patient have a limit}.
221: {Jack Dempsey bobbed and weaved in a figure eight, and every turn of the head launched a hook | The Manassa Mauler won the title in Toledo in 1919 by putting Willard on the floor seven times in a round}. {Weave, hook, weave, hook, and the rhythm never stops | The roll builds, and every turn feeds the next | Six hooks, and the last one is the heaviest}. {Roll | Keep rolling}.
222: {The acrobat's last leap is the one that cannot be undone | Death-defying, the circus posters said, and meant that death was watching}. {All of me, through the air, onto one target | Only the impact matters | I leap, and let the fall take care of itself}. {Now | Everything on one jump}.
223: {Nirvana is the blowing out of the flame, and the monk who reaches its edge cannot be extinguished | The Buddha sat under the bodhi tree and Mara's armies could not move him}. {At the edge of nirvana, death has no hold on me | The flame is calm, and nothing can blow it out | The body is restored, and the spirit beyond reach}. {Untouchable | I stand at the threshold, and I do not fall}.
224: {The knockout punch is the dream of every boxer and the nightmare of every opponent | When the man is nearly gone, the knockout finishes him clean}. {This one ends it | All the fight in one fist | One punch, one count, one champion}. {Knockout | Ten}.
236: {Fiore set the lynx above the lion, the tiger and the elephant, for no strength outlives the eye that keeps watch | Stand before them, says the master, and let your body be the wall they cannot raise | The first oath of the sword is owed to the one who stands behind you}. {Whoever falls first falls through me | My body is the guard, and the blade only its gate | Strike here, and here alone}. {No one passes while I stand | The line holds because I hold it}.
237: {Marozzo taught that the mandritto and the roverso are one wheel, and a wheel does not stop | Forehand, backhand, and never the guard between them | Seven cuts, and each one the preparation of the next}. {Give him no breath to answer with | Strike until his lungs surrender before his hands do | The storm does not ask whether the field is ready}. {Do not return to guard. There is nothing to return to | When the seventh lands, the first is still falling}.
238: {Young knight, learn to love God and honour women, so begins the Zettel of Liechtenauer | Kneel to God, stand for the lord, bleed for the man beside you | Be without fear before your enemies, runs the vow of every knight}. {Steady the shield, clear the eye, and let every blow be the true one | Fear narrows the hand; resolve opens it | There is one cut that matters, and today we all make it}. {We do not yield | Hold, and strike true}.
239: {Hayashizaki Jinsuke prayed a hundred days at the shrine of Hayashi Myojin and rose with the draw that bears his art | Saya no uchi: the victory is won while the blade still sleeps in the scabbard | The sword that is drawn is already late; the sword that draws and cuts is already done}. {Sit still. Breathe once. Let him come to the edge | The strong are cut; the dying are released | One motion from scabbard to scabbard, and nothing remains to finish}.
240: {Capo Ferro measured the lunge to the breadth of a finger and set the point where he had measured | The point travels the shortest line, and the shortest line is the one never seen | Strike the gap in the plate}. {Find the vein, find the seam, find the open door | A hand's width of steel, placed truly, outweighs an arm's length of edge}.
241: {Talhoffer drew the murder-stroke: the sword reversed, the pommel swung as a hammer | Where the edge cannot bite through steel, the pommel breaks it | Grip the blade, and the pommel becomes the mace}. {Break the guard and the man behind it follows | Steel on the helm, and the helm rings his ruin}.
242: {The Bolognese call it the molinello, the mill wheel that grinds whatever falls into it | Turn once, and every foe in reach stands inside the same answer | The circle is closed, and the circle is guarded}. {Come at me now, and the wheel turns back on you | I end where I began, blade ready, waiting for the next}.
243: {Vadi wrote that geometry divides the sword, and the sword divides the man | First the wound is opened, then the wound is entered | Look once, strike once, at the place already shown}. {Where the heart is bared, the sword does not hesitate | The second blow is the one that was promised}.
244: {Liechtenauer called it the Vor: the first strike, taken before the foe has drawn his breath | Who strikes after must defend; who strikes before is already defended | Be first, and be certain}. {The blade is out and back before his weight arrives | His arm learns fear before it learns the blow}. {Never wait | Strike first}.
245: {Meyer drilled the crossing strokes until the cuts fell like the arms of a cross | Two lines across one body, and the body remembers both | The first cut writes; the second signs}. {Where blood already runs, the cross opens it wider | Cross him, and let him carry the mark to the earth}.
246: {The whole arm, the whole body, the whole rank | The Italians scorn the wide cut in their prose and draw it in their plates, for it wins fields | Give all, and keep nothing back for the return}. {The line breaks and the line falls | Let them stagger; the weight of the blade does the rest}.
247: {Draw the edge; a drawn cut keeps working long after the sword has gone | The sabre masters taught the draw, and the draw is how a small wound wins a long fight | Open the vein and let time finish}. {He will bleed while he thinks of his answer | Every heartbeat now fights for me}.
248: {Fiore's first rule: never offer what you cannot take back | Cut from behind the guard, and remain behind it | The guard is the shadow of the strike}. {Strike, and be already closed | He finds steel where he sought an opening}.
249: {The plainest cut in every manual, and the one every master trusts last | Down the line, across the rank, without ornament | No secret, no art, only the edge and the will}. {The stumbling are mown like wheat | Those who have lost their feet will lose more}.
250: {Above the head the blade turns twice, and the air itself is drawn into the turning | The mill sail gathers whatever wind comes | Spin, and let the gale carry the edge where it will}. {Three are struck, and none saw whence it came | The wind is the second blade}.
251: {Below the knee, where no plate is fitted, because no man can walk in it | Take the legs, and the rest of him will kneel | The ground is an ally to whoever reaches it first}. {Root torn, the tree leans | A man who cannot stand cannot fight}.
252: {Nachreisen, the Germans named it: travel after him, and strike as he recovers | Wait for the opening; when it comes, there is no waiting left | Patience is a blade, sharpened in silence}. {The door he opened, I walk through | The moment is given once. Take it whole}.
253: {Into the press, the point seeking whoever stands nearest | When the field is chaos, the point becomes chaos too | Four thrusts, four foes, and fortune chooses the throats}. {Let the crowd find my point | In the melee, every direction is forward}.
254: {The blade becomes a storm, and the storm a circle | Musashi wrote a Book of Wind; this is the wind itself | Turn until the air screams along the edge}. {What stumbles is torn apart | The arms that would rise are beaten down by the gale}.
255: {The flat is a choice: the man shall live, but he shall not stand | Trial by combat sometimes demanded the accused alive, and the flat delivered him so | Not every foe has earned the edge}. {The skull rings, and the world goes dark | Sleep, and remember who spared you}.
256: {Fabris kept the point on the line and moved the whole body around it | From the elbow, one thrust behind the next, and the line never breaks | The point does not leave him between blows}. {Six times the steel arrives, six times the arm grows weaker | He cannot parry what does not stop}.
257: {Shield to shield the Spartans stood at Thermopylae, and the pass held three days | Close the line. Every shield guards the man to its left | The phalanx is a wall that breathes}. {Lock shields | Not one step back}.
258: {Thibault inscribed the descending line in his great circle; the falcon knew it long before | From above the guard, faster than the eye can follow | The falcon does not circle twice}. {Strike from the height and lay the heart open | Before he looks up, it is over}.
259: {Once to ask, twice to answer | The first thrust finds the line; the second rides it home | The Italian books draw it again and again: the double thrust, and the opening it leaves behind}. {And now the true blow waits | He parried the first. There was always a second}.
260: {The Oberhau is the first cut taught and the last abandoned | From the roof, with all the shoulders hold, and nothing kept back | Raise it high; let heaven and the arm fall together}. {The staggering man looks up only once | No neck is braced for what falls from above}.
261: {The Zornhau, the stroke of wrath, from the shoulder to the opposite hip | Whoever strikes at you from above, the point of the wrath stroke threatens him, sings Liechtenauer}. {Simple. True. Enough | The first cut a student learns, and the last one he forgets}.
262: {Mikazuki Munechika, finest of the Five Swords Under Heaven, carries crescent moons in its temper | The curved blade cuts by travelling, as the crescent travels the night | One long arc beneath the moon, laid across the whole line}. {Every wound a thin moon, and every moon bleeds | Their strength runs out with their blood}.
263: {Ringen am Schwert: when the swords are too close for the edge, the earth becomes the weapon | Down, and down again, until the man and the ground are one | Bring the weight, and bring him with it}. {Stay where I put you | The earth holds him for me}.
264: {Sword blessings survive in old monastery books, spoken over the steel before the vigil | Speak to the blade before you swing it, and it answers in fire | The rune is laid along the fuller, and the fuller fills with flame}. {Burn, and remember the hand that lit you | Steel and fire, one oath}.
265: {The glyph is cut into the foe, and through it his power runs out | Each sign carved by the point is a mouth that drinks | A circuit closes along the edge, and the current flows to me}. {What you gathered is mine now | Your mana feeds my blade}.
266: {Rise from below the guard, where the helm is only laced | Every harness has a seam beneath the chin | From the knee to the jaw in one line}. {His sight swims, and his aim with it | Let his thoughts scatter like his teeth}.
267: {Drawn from the stone, returned to the lake: the sword of the rightful king | Caliburnus, Geoffrey of Monmouth named it, forged in the isle of Avalon | By the sword that chooses its bearer}. {Let the unworthy fall before the light | Holy steel finds no armour it must respect}.
268: {Into the centre of them, and turning | Enter the rank and break it from within | No guard holds against what is already inside the guard}. {Shields split, and the line splits with them | Let them hear their armour crack}.
269: {Capo Ferro's lunge: the whole body behind one point, and no road home | All, or nothing | Commit everything, and keep nothing for defence}. {If I fall, I fall through him | There is no second blow; there need not be}.
270: {The way of the warrior is found in dying, says the Hagakure; then fear is already spent | Gi, yu, jin, rei, makoto, meiyo, chugi: seven virtues and one blade | Think of nothing but the cutting, Musashi taught}. {Clear minds, quick hands | Rise, and let the spirit carry the steel}.
271: {The shield is raised over the realm, and the realm stands behind it | One shield for one man; one vow for a whole people | The Roman scutum covered one soldier; the wall of them covered an empire}. {Whatever curse they laid on you is lifted here | Stand beneath the banner, and be whole}.
272: {The estoc was forged for one purpose: to find the gap in the plate | Armour is passed by | What stops the edge does not stop the spike}. {Your steel is no shelter | Through the mail, through the plate, through the man}.
273: {Fear the man who has thrown one cut ten thousand times | A thousand days to forge, ten thousand days to polish, wrote Musashi | The one technique practised more than all the others combined}. {There is no surprise in it, and no answer either | This is what the years were for}.
274: {Enough weight behind the edge that the guard is only a formality | The falchion was a peasant's blade, and it cleaved knights | Cleave the steel, and the arm beneath it}. {Mass needs no cleverness | Let the sword carry its own verdict}.
275: {The Posta di Donna, Fiore's guard of the woman, from which every cut and thrust may be thrown | From the Lady's Guard the point flies, and the body follows like water | Grace is mastery}. {Move as the river, and nothing will hold you | I am already where your blow is not}.
276: {Past the limit the body sets, and past the pain that guards it | Every tradition keeps one technique that wounds its user, and teaches it anyway | Burn what you were saving}. {The body breaks; the blow does not | Give it everything, and then give more}.
277: {The spell is laid along the edge and travels with it | Runes inlaid in the steel, names of power older than the blade | Cut through the ward, and the warded fall}. {Your blessings end here | Every enchantment unravels at the edge}.
278: {The runes are carved, the runes are charged, the runes are loosed | Fire written into steel waits only for the word | Each rune a spark, each spark a pyre}. {Burn | Let the rank become embers}.
279: {More cuts than a single motion can hold, delivered within a single motion | The blade is in many places, and the man in one | Forbidden, because it cannot be taught without a death}. {The falling are cut a hundred times before they land | When the dust settles, he has already been answered}.
280: {The boss is iron because the boss is a weapon; the rest of the shield is a door | Drive the face of the shield into his guard, and the guard is gone | Defence, used as it was always meant to be used}. {Break, and fall back | The wall advances}.
281: {Look at me. Only at me | The champion steps forward so that no one behind him must | Offer him the open line, and own whatever answer comes}. {Come, if you dare | Here is your enemy}.
282: {Blade and spell in turn, too swift for either to be named | The guild calls them two arts; the hand knows only one | Steel, then sigil, then steel again}. {Guard against one, and the other arrives | Their feet grow heavy under the storm}.
283: {The core is driven past every limit and vented outward | Blood and mana, burned together in one breath | Overload is the purpose}. {What I spend of myself, they pay twice over | Their defences open under the flood}.
284: {A sword that was a spell long before it was a sword | The magi who followed the star carried blades that answered it | Edge and art land together on the whole rank}. {Now the true spells begin | The power rises with every cut}.
285: {Steel and sorcery collapse toward one point, and the point is doom | Where the two arts meet, a darkness gathers | All force drawn into one seam, then released}. {You are marked; there is no hiding now | Death knows your name}.
286: {Nothing passes while the line holds | Mind and body sealed alike: no poison, no curse, no fear | The wall that guards the body guards the soul as well}. {Let them throw their worst | We are unbroken}.
287: {The aegis of Athena, borne once over heroes, is raised again | Votive shields hung in the temples for centuries, and came down when the old enemies returned | A shield older than the war it is carried through}. {The ancients stand with us | No blow lands true beneath this cover}.
299: {The deep things wear no armour; they wear the slick of the sea floor, and nothing keeps its grip | Aldrovandi kept the slime of a nameless creature sealed in glass in Bologna, and it never dried}. {Let them stand on it, and learn how quickly the ground forsakes the proud | Cover them, and their footing is mine}.
300: {One drop is a sentence, and the fang does not argue it | The serpent strikes once and waits, for the venom does the rest}. {Small wound, long dying | Patience is the second fang}.
301: {The whale sings across an ocean, and the same song can stop a heart | Cardano heard through his teeth what the ear refused; the beast sings to the bone}. {Let the deep note roll over the line, and the water in their blood answer it | No hand is raised; the song breaks them}.
302: {The bear-shirted ones of the north bit their shields and felt no steel | Odin's wolves wore no mail, and fire and iron could not touch them}. {Let the pain go silent and the blood go loud | No fear, no mercy, no tomorrow}.
303: {The bright frog carries death on its skin and fears no hand | Colour is the warning; the poison is the promise}. {Touch me and your limbs forget you | What the venom takes, the body does not give back}.
304: {The bat sees with its voice; turn that voice upon a man and he sees nothing true | One cry, and up becomes down}. {The ground tilts, the sky turns, and they fall where they stand | Let them stagger; I will be waiting where they land}.
305: {The spider's thread is finer than hair and stronger than iron | Vine, silk or tentacle, the binding is the same oath}. {Struggle, and the web holds tighter | What is caught is already eaten}.
306: {The banshee's cry was a beast's before it was a ghost's | High and thin, the scream that splits the mind}. {Let no prayer be spoken and no thought be whole | Their voices drown in mine}.
307: {The salamander walks through fire and its wounds close behind it | The body is its own apothecary, and the old beasts never forgot the recipe}. {Lick the wound and live | The scent of blood calls the hunter; let it come}.
308: {The cuttlefish becomes the stone, and the stone does not move | Be the leaf, be the shadow, be nothing at all}. {The eye that hunts me finds only the world | Unseen is unhurt}.
